title: Who Is Théo?
summary: Weeks three and four. Learning to be alone without being lonely, and finding the {man|woman|person} underneath "we". The second half unlocks after a real walk somewhere new. Ends with 5 lights.

screens.image: Théo's kitchen, black, with the warm lights from earlier chapters glowing in the background. Two plates on the counter.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Week three. Théo cooks dinner, sets out two plates, and only then notices.

screens.image: Close-up: the two plates, one of them slowly fading out.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: For two years, Théo cooked for two. And only what Lisa liked: no coriander, no spice, nothing with a bone in it.

screens.image: Théo standing alone, holding a pan.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {He|She|They} {realises|realises|realise} {he|she|they} {doesn't|doesn't|don't} know what {he|she|they} {likes|likes|like} to cook anymore. Or what {he|she|they} {likes|likes|like} at all.

screens.image: The Critic sitting on the counter, size 5.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: You didn't have a personality. You had a girlfriend.

screens.image: Théo looking at the Critic.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: That isn't true. It's just loud.

interaction.explainer: You can't argue the Critic away. But you can answer it.

screens.image: The Critic one size smaller.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Smaller. Not gone. Smaller.

screens.image: Marie-Clo's office, the warm lamp.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Who were you before her? Not your job. Not the {chased}. You.

screens.image: Théo shrugging, a speech bubble with a question mark.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: I don't know. I used to cook a lot. I used to... I don't know.

screens.image: Marie-Clo handing {him|her|them} a big sheet of paper: a hand-drawn map with an empty centre labelled "Théo".

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Then let's find out. A little each week.

screens.image: The Who Is Théo? map: a hand-drawn island with four regions: Things I love / Things I used to love / Things I'm curious about / Things I'm good at.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The Who Is Théo? map. It starts almost empty. That's normal. Lisa's face isn't on it. This one is only {his|hers|theirs}.

interaction.prompt: Add at least one thing, to any region.

screens.image: The map with the player's items drawn as little landmarks (a pan, a tree, a ball).

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It will grow. Every chapter adds to it.

screens.image: A page of lined paper, a pen.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Marie-Clo gave {him|her|them} one more experiment. Write five sentences about this month, but not with "I". With {his|her|their} own name.

screens.image: Same paper, an example in cream handwriting.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: "Théo is having a hard month. Théo is sad, and {he's|she's|they're} also still cooking. Théo is..."

interaction.prompt: Write five sentences about your own week, using your own name.

screens.image: The paper folded into a paper boat.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It's a strange trick. Talking about yourself by name puts a little distance between you and the pain, like looking at your life from across the street. Scientists have measured it: it calms the part of the brain that loops.

screens.image: Night. Théo in bed, the phone glowing cold blue. A wave shape rising over the bed.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: At 1am, the wanting comes. To check her profile. To see if she's okay. To see if she's not okay.

screens.image: A big hand-drawn wave rising and falling.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: This feeling is like a wave. It rises, peaks, and falls on its own, in about a minute and a half. You don't have to fight it. Just ride it.

screens.image: The wave flat. The phone dark.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Did the wave pass?

options.label: Put the phone in the kitchen

screens.image: Phone screen, cold blue, Théo small.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {He|She|They} {checks|checks|check}. She looks fine. That's the worst and best news at once. Théo feels worse. That's allowed. Tomorrow is a new night.

screens.image: Phone on the kitchen counter, Théo asleep.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {He|She|They} {sleeps|sleeps|sleep} badly. But {he|she|they} {sleeps|sleeps|sleep}.

screens.image: A small box with a clock on it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Some worries come at all hours. Marie-Clo's trick: give them an appointment. Write them down, and save them for one fixed time of day. Fifteen minutes. Then the box closes.

interaction.prompt: Worry box: put today's worries in here. They'll keep until their appointment.

screens.image: A city map with one part of town in shadow, never visited.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Last thing. Théo has lived here two years and only ever walked Lisa's routes. Her café, her market, her friends' street.

screens.image: Quest card, with a small drawn path into the unknown.

interaction.title: Somewhere new
interaction.text: Go for a walk somewhere you've never walked, alone, on purpose. Twenty minutes is enough. Look up at least once.

screens.image: A park with huge plane trees, early morning fog. The trees drawn in pencil grey, not black. The first grey that isn't darkness.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo walks to the park on the other side of the river. {He|She|They} {has|has|have} never been here. Nobody here has ever seen {him|her|them} with Lisa.

screens.image: Looking up through the plane tree branches; a big pale sky.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {He|She|They} {looks|looks|look} up. The trees are two hundred years old. They have seen a lot of people walk under them with a broken heart. They are still here.

screens.image: A scruffy three-legged dog running at Théo, tongue out.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Then a dog arrives. A dog with three legs and no shame.

screens.image: Sophie in a yellow raincoat, running after the dog, laughing. The yellow raincoat glows.

words.speaker: Sophie
words.text: Trois-Pattes! Sorry, sorry. He thinks everyone is his friend.

screens.image: Théo kneeling, scratching the dog's ears.
Sophie talking, Trois-Pattes rolling on his back.

words.speaker: Sophie
words.text: A car, when he was a puppy. He never noticed he was missing one. He's the happiest one in the park.

interaction.text: Sophie: walks Trois-Pattes here every morning. He lost his leg as a puppy and never noticed.

screens.image: Sophie and the dog walking away into fog, the yellow coat glowing.

words.speaker: Sophie
words.text: Same time every day, if you want to meet him again.

screens.image: The map from 3.20, the park now drawn in, a small yellow light in it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo didn't plan to talk to anyone. The world sent a dog.

screens.image: Théo at his window that night. Two questions in cream letters float over the dark city.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Marie-Clo asks {him|her|them} to choose one place to go back to, again and again. Two questions help: How much energy does Théo have? And {does|does|do} {he|she|they} want to talk, or just be near people?

screens.image: Quest card.

interaction.title: Pick your place
interaction.text: Choose one real place you could go to every week: a café, library, park, club, class. Write its name.
